_comment: Mutation-tests the pure hexagon (domain + mappers + use-cases) against the node:test suites run via tsx. The command runner re-runs `npm run test:domain` per mutant. timeoutMS is deliberately generous: Stryker allows 1.5 x netTime + timeoutMS, the suite takes ~4.4s alone but ~28s with `concurrency` runs in flight, and at the previous 20000 that landed just under the limit — so 41% of mutants were recorded as timeouts. A timeout scores as killed, so that did not just add noise, it hid real survivors and inflated the score (volume-mapper.ts read 94.23% with 38 timeouts; with a workable timeout it is 80.77% with 10 survivors and none). Thresholds are set to what the suite actually holds rather than to a comfortable default: break at 98, because the surviving mutants are provably equivalent and are disabled at the site with their reasoning, so a drop below that is a real regression rather than noise. 100% is not the target — deciding mutant equivalence is undecidable in general, and chasing the last few would mean tests that assert states Kubernetes cannot produce.
